outcome: success of assisted vaginal rotational delivery
cohort: 838 births with malposition of the fetal head complicating the second stage of labor
finding: The study found that obstetricians were more likely to deem assisted vaginal delivery unsafe for babies in occiput posterior position compared to occiput transverse position, leading to higher rates of primary emergency cesarean section in the former group.
mod_finding: When vaginal delivery was deemed safe, the success rate of the first attempted instrumental delivery was similar between occiput posterior and occiput transverse positions (74.4% vs. 79.3%).
